1.1.37 — A real browser

  • Sign in with Google, Apple and more. Sign-in popups now open in their own small window, linked to the site that opened them, so the login comes back to the page and the popup closes itself.
  • Page dialogs and uploads. Sites' alerts, confirmations and questions now show up, and “Choose File” buttons open the file picker.
  • Drag and drop. Drop links or files on the sidebar to open them in new tabs, or on a new tab to open them there. PDFs, pictures and saved pages open right in Pane.
  • Print. ⌘P prints the page.
  • Sites that ask for a password now show a sign-in sheet instead of failing.
  • Camera, microphone and location. Video calls, voice messages and maps can ask to use them, as in Safari.

1.1.36 — Tabs stay awake, swipe flipped

  • Tabs stay awake when you leave them. 1.1.35 put tabs to sleep too soon. Now a tab sleeps only after you've been away for the time set in Settings › Tabs, or when your Mac is really short of memory. Recent tabs switch instantly again, so memory stays higher until tabs start to sleep.
  • Swipe direction flipped. Two fingers right now goes forward and two fingers left goes back. The glass arrow moves with your fingers.

1.1.35 — Lighter and smoother

  • Much less memory. Only your current tab and the one before it stay ready. Others sleep, and they sleep sooner, so a handful of busy sites takes about half the memory it did.
  • Tabs wake where you left them. A sleeping tab comes back at the same spot with its Back history, showing a picture of the page until it's ready.
  • Gives memory back. When your Mac runs short, tabs out of view go to sleep right away. Tabs playing video or in a call stay awake.
  • Quiet when idle. The New Tab page no longer works in the background, so Pane uses almost no power when you're not using it.
  • A smoother sidebar. The page keeps its size while the sidebar slides, so the slide stutters far less.
